assumptions: Projection is validated and carried but not materialised: this engine returns the item's body for any enumerated projection, because deriving views is a projection-engine job. Stated as a limit in SPEC.md section 10; a host that derives views supplies them as their own items.

A JSON pointer selects a region only in a JSON body; the selected value is canonicalised (sort_keys, ','/':' separators) and stored as its own content identity. Plain-text region addressing is not implemented.
The per-turn resolve budget is counted against the ledger handed to resolve(); a host wanting a per-turn budget passes a fresh ledger per turn (file may persist for the session).

The repository root is found by walking up from the engine's own file for '.git' or 'pyproject.toml' (found: /home/zer0null/reserach extarctor). If no marker exists the engine refuses nothing, so a vendored copy outside any repo still works.
Python 3.11+ assumed (uses dataclasses, pathlib.is_relative_to); executed on CPython 3.14.4 with pytest 9.0.2. No third-party dependency.

The ledger row carries two optional keys beyond the contracted set -- 'ref' (text as presented) and 'ref_index' (the index's spelling of the same entry) -- because a caller may omit a revision the index pins and the adapter must still recognise the resolve. Documented in SPEC.md section 7; all contracted keys are present in every row.

Corpus for the worked example is exactly 12 items and exactly 30,000 characters, chosen to sit at the measured crossover rather than to flatter the ratio; r = 67.1x is a property of 12 index lines over 30,000 bytes at ~2.5 KB per body, not a universal constant.
Warmpool roots in tests come from pytest tmp_path, which resolves under /tmp and is asserted (conftest, session-autouse) to be outside the repository before any test runs.
